examples.problem_statement: Using synthetic division, find the quotient and remainder when $2x^4 - 3x^3 - 6x^2 + 11x - 10$ is divided by $x - 2$.

solution.operation: Write the coefficients of the polynomial: $2$, $-3$, $-6$, $11$, $-10$.
Set up synthetic division with the zero of $x-2$, which is $2$.
Multiply $2$ by $2$ to get $4$, add to $-3$ to get $1$.
Multiply $1$ by $2$ to get $2$, add to $-6$ to get $-4$.
Multiply $-4$ by $2$ to get $-8$, add to $11$ to get $3$.
Multiply $3$ by $2$ to get $6$, add to $-10$ to get $-4$ (remainder).
The numbers $2, 1, -4, 3$ are the coefficients of the quotient: $2x^3 + x^2 - 4x + 3$, and the last number $-4$ is the remainder.
Set up synthetic division with root 2: | 1  5  -7  -13  -2 | 2
Multiply 1 by 2 = 2, add to next coefficient: 5 + 2 = 7
Multiply 7 by 2 = 14, add to next coefficient: -7 + 14 = 7
Multiply 7 by 2 = 14, add to next coefficient: -13 + 14 = 1
Multiply 1 by 2 = 2, add to last term: -2 + 2 = 0
Set up synthetic division with the root of the divisor $x - 2 = 0$, which is $2$.
Write down the coefficients of the dividend: $2, -3, -6, 11, -10$.
Multiply $3$ by $2$ to get $6$, add to $-10$ to get $-4$.
The bottom row gives the coefficients of the quotient and the remainder. The quotient is $2x^3 + x^2 - 4x + 3$ and the remainder is $-4$.

examples.problem_statement: A ball is projected upward from the ground at an angle 60° from the horizontal with initial velocity 60 ft/s. Find (a) the time it will be in the air (b) its range, that is, the horizontal distance it will travel, and (c) its maximum height attained.

solution.description: Split the 60 ft/s launch speed into the two directions that behave differently: horizontally 60 cos 60 degrees gives 30 ft/s, vertically 60 sin 60 degrees gives 30 root 3 ft/s. Every later step works on one component at a time.

Turn those components into position-versus-time equations. Nothing acts horizontally, so x grows steadily at 30 ft/s, while vertically gravity subtracts one half of 32 t squared, that is 16 t squared, from the rising 30 root 3 t.

solution.operation: Find time of flight (when ball returns to ground, y=0)
solution.description: The ball is on the ground exactly when the vertical position is zero, so factor that equation. One root, t = 0, is the launch instant; the other, 15 root 3 over 8 seconds, is the landing time asked for in part (a).

solution.operation: Calculate range (horizontal distance at time of flight)
solution.description: Range is how far the steady horizontal drift carries the ball during that flight, so put the time 15 root 3 over 8 into x = 30t, giving 225 root 3 over 4 feet.

solution.operation: Find maximum height using time to reach apex
solution.description: The ball is highest at the instant it stops climbing, so set the vertical velocity 30 root 3 minus 32 t equal to zero. That gives t = 15 root 3 over 16 seconds, exactly half the flight time found in step 3.
Feed that apex time back into the vertical position equation. The rising term contributes 1350 over 16 and gravity takes back 675 over 16, leaving a maximum height of 675 over 16 feet.

Finally, note the shortcut this long computation has just confirmed: for any quadratic a x squared plus b x plus c the derivative is 2 a x plus b. With a = 4 and b = 3 that reads off 8x + 3 at once, matching the limit result of step 6, and the constant 5 simply drops out.

key_reminders: {'point': "In problem 45.9(c): 'Identify the given point on the parabola.' In problem 45.11: '(Why should P not be taken at an extremity of the major axis?)'"}
common_mistakes: Differentiating 4 x squared as 4 x. The coefficient must be multiplied by the exponent, giving 8x.
Carrying the constant 5 into the answer. A constant contributes nothing once f(x + delta x) minus f(x) is taken, as step 4 shows.
Cancelling delta x from the quotient before every term of the numerator carries a factor of delta x, which loses the 4 delta x squared term that vanishes only in the limit.
repair_note: Rewrote the step 7 description, which trailed off mid-sentence ('For , derivative is') and narrated the power rule in isolation instead of the shortcut its own result 2 a x plus b states. Steps 1 through 6 were already correct for their operations and were left alone.
